label: Fleet Simulation
info:
Node-RED simulation of the driverless taxi fleet.

One sedan (TAXI-001, home Melbourne CBD), one van (TAXI-002, home Sunshine), one bus (TAXI-003, fixed Boxhill-Camberwell-Burwood loop). Vehicles move along the graph/melbourne.json road network, loaded via settings.js functionGlobalContext.

Telemetry path: tick -> Fleet Sensor Simulator (per-type payload) -> Edge Filter -> MQTT publish (fleet/<vehicleID>/telemetry) + debug.
Actuator path: MQTT subscribe (fleet/+/command) or manual inject -> Actuator Controller -> debug. A dispatch command carries a node-id route; the sedan or van drives it and parks at the pickup node.

name: Telemetry simulation
info:
# Fleet Sensor Simulator

Each tick every vehicle emits a telemetry packet whose shape depends on `vehicleType` (see `schema/telemetry.schema.json`).

Common fields: `vehicleID`, `vehicleType`, `coordinates{lat,lon}`, `heading`, `speed`, `batteryLevel`, `currentState` (driving | parked | charging), `timestamp` (Unix ms, stamped at the edge).

- **sedan**: `occupancy{seatsTotal,seatsOccupied,seatWeightKg}`, `doorsLocked`
- **van**: `occupancy{...}`, `doorState{front,slidingLeft,rear}`, `cargoLoadKg`
- **bus**: `passengerCount`, `passengerCapacity`, `doorState{front,middle,rear}`, `wheelchairRampDeployed`, `nextStopId`

Dispatchable vehicles (sedan, van) idle at their home node until a dispatch command gives them a node route. The bus runs its loop continuously.

name: Fleet Sensor Simulator
Edge Filter (stationary + GPS delta < 0.0001)
MQTT broker
info:
# MQTT (Weeks 4 and 6)

Broker: Eclipse Mosquitto on `localhost:1883` (repo-root `docker-compose.yml`).

- **out**: forwarded telemetry is published to `fleet/<vehicleID>/telemetry`.
- **in**: `fleet/+/command` is subscribed and fed to the Actuator Controller.

The Event Router (`services/event-router`) consumes `fleet/+/telemetry`, validates each payload against `schema/telemetry.schema.json`, and re-publishes valid packets on `validated/<vehicleID>/telemetry`. The Dispatch service (`services/dispatch-service`) publishes the `dispatch` commands with an A* node route.

name: Actuator commands
info:
# Actuators

Simulated motor controller + door lock. Commands `{ vehicleID, command, route?, passengers? }` where command is one of `dispatch`, `stop`, `lock_doors`, `unlock_doors` arrive over MQTT on `fleet/+/command` (from the Dispatch service) or from the inject nodes here. `dispatch` makes the vehicle follow the node-id route; `stop` clears it. Responses go to the debug sidebar.
